newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan top banks unveil BIS capital adequacy ratios.
newsitem.headline: Japan top banks unveil BIS capital adequacy ratios.

text.p: Japan's top 20 commercial banks on Monday disclosed their preliminary international capital adequacy ratios at the end of the financial year on March 31.
Capital adequacy ratios were as follows (with a year-ago comparisons):
Under the rules of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Japanese banks operating internationally need to have capital equivalent to eight percent of risk-weighted assets.
Unlike many countries, Japanese authorities allow banks to include unrealised profits on securities holdings as part of capital.

The full names of the banks are Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, Sumitomo Bank Ltd, Sanwa Bank Ltd, Sakura Bank Ltd, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd (BOT-Mitsubishi), Fuji Bank Ltd, Tokai Bank Ltd, Asahi Bank Ltd, Daiwa Bank Ltd, and Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd, Mitsui Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Trust & Banking Corp, Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Yasuda Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Nippon Trust Bank Ltd, Toyo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Chuo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ), the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd.
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi was formed in April 1996 as result of a merger of Mitsubishi Bank Ltd and Bank of Tokyo Ltd.
